mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, or SPX posts negative 60-day returns in > 60% of quarters with YoY GDP acceleration > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a supply-driven inflationary shock that will pressure the Fed to tighten policy and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month, and UNRATE does not rise > 0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or the Fed cuts rates within 3 months of the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in nonfarm payrolls, if accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate, signals a tightening labor market that will boost wage growth and consumption, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 200k in 1 month, and UNRATE declines > 0.1pp in the same month
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or real wage growth fails to accelerate in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A surprise rate hike by the Fed, defined as a 25bp increase in the federal funds rate that is not fully priced in by the futures market, signals a hawkish policy shift that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 1 month, and the hike was not fully priced in by the futures market 1 week prior
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or the Fed reverses course with a rate cut within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in housing starts, if accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate, signals a strengthening housing market and labor market that will boost consumption and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 5% YoY, and UNRATE declines > 0.5pp over the same period
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or housing affordability deteriorates due to rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the consumer price index, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in industrial production, signals a cost-push inflationary shock that will pressure corporate margins and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month, and INDPRO does not rise > 0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or the Fed does not respond with a rate hike within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, if accompanied by a decline in retail sales, signals a weakening labor market and consumption that will produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, and RSAFS declines > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or initial jobless claims do not rise further in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate, if accompanied by a rise in the consumer price index, signals a dovish policy shift that will boost risk appetite and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines > 0.5pp in 3 months, and CPIAUCSL rises > 1% over the same period
failure_condition: SPX posts negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or the Fed reverses course with a rate hike within 6 months.
